title: 🔥 Forgiveness from the Cross: What Jesus’ Words Teach Us Today!
paragraphs: 🔥 Forgiveness from the Cross: What Jesus’ Words Teach Us Today!

"Imagine being tortured, humiliated, and sentenced to die for a crime you never committed. The very people you came to save mock you, spit on you, and drive nails into your hands. What would your last words be?"

📖 Luke 23:34 (KJV):
"Then said Jesus, Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do. And they parted his raiment, and cast lots."

❓ READER QUESTION:
"Brother John, how could Jesus forgive the very people who crucified Him? And what does this mean for us today?"

🚨 THE TRUTH: What This Blog Will Reveal!
✔️ Why Jesus chose to forgive His executioners.
✔️ The deeper spiritual meaning behind His words.
✔️ How this moment fulfilled ancient prophecies.
✔️ How we are also guilty—but Jesus offers us the same forgiveness!

WHY DID JESUS CHOOSE TO FORGIVE?
Many people struggle to forgive those who hurt them. Yet, Jesus—while hanging on the cross—chose to forgive the very ones who crucified Him!

📖 Luke 23:34 (KJV):
"Then said Jesus, Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do."
💡 THE TRUTH:

Jesus was experiencing unimaginable pain, humiliation, and betrayal.
Instead of calling down fire from heaven or condemning His enemies, He chose mercy.
This was not weakness—it was the ultimate display of divine love and grace!
🚨 THE WARNING: If Jesus forgave those who crucified Him, what excuse do we have to hold grudges?

THE DEEPER MEANING BEHIND JESUS’ WORDS!
Jesus’ words were not just about the Romans or the Pharisees. They had a greater spiritual meaning!

📖 John 3:17 (KJV):
"For God sent not his Son into the world to condemn the world; but that the world through him might be saved."
💡 WHO DID JESUS FORGIVE?

✔ 1️⃣ THE ROMAN SOLDIERS – They executed Jesus but had no idea they were killing the Son of God!
✔ 2️⃣ THE PHARISEES & JEWISH LEADERS – They conspired to crucify Jesus, believing they were defending God’s law.
✔ 3️⃣ THE CROWD WHO SHOUTED ‘CRUCIFY HIM!’ – They blindly followed the religious leaders without understanding the truth.
✔ 4️⃣ US – ALL HUMANITY! – Jesus wasn’t just forgiving those at the cross—He was forgiving all of us!
🚨 THE WARNING: Without Jesus’ forgiveness, we would all be condemned!

PROPHECY FULFILLED – JESUS’ WORDS WERE FORETOLD!
Jesus’ prayer of forgiveness was not random—it was a fulfillment of ancient prophecy!

📖 Isaiah 53:12 (KJV):
"And he bare the sin of many, and made intercession for the transgressors."
💡 PROPHECIES FULFILLED:

✔ 1️⃣ Isaiah 53:5 – "He was wounded for our transgressions."
🔥 Jesus suffered in our place to bring us peace!

✔ 2️⃣ Psalm 22:16 – "They pierced my hands and my feet."
🔥 This prophecy describes crucifixion—hundreds of years before it was even invented!

✔ 3️⃣ Micah 7:18 – "Who is a God like unto thee, that pardoneth iniquity?"
🔥 Only God could offer forgiveness even to His enemies!
🚨 THE WARNING: Jesus didn’t just forgive because He wanted to—He forgave because it was God’s divine plan from the beginning!

GREEK & HEBREW WORD ANALYSIS – DEEPER BIBLICAL REVELATION!
Understanding the original biblical words gives us deeper insight into Jesus’ prayer of forgiveness.

🔥 GREEK WORD ANALYSIS – "FORGIVE" (ἀφίημι – Aphiemi)
📖 Luke 23:34 (KJV):
"Then said Jesus, Father, forgive (Aphiemi) them; for they know not what they do."
💡 Meaning in Greek:

Aphiemi means "to release, to send away, to cancel a debt."
Jesus was not just saying, "Ignore their sin"—He was asking God to cancel their punishment!
🚨 THE LESSON: If Jesus asked God to cancel the punishment of His enemies, how much more should we forgive those who hurt us?

🔥 HEBREW WORD ANALYSIS – "KNOW" (יָדַע – Yada’)
📖 Luke 23:34 (KJV):
"For they know (Yada’) not what they do."
💡 Meaning in Hebrew:

Yada’ means "to know, to perceive, to understand deeply."
Jesus was saying that His enemies lacked true spiritual understanding of their actions.
🚨 THE LESSON: Many people reject God simply because they don’t know the truth—our job is to pray for them, not hate them!

PROOF & HISTORICAL EVIDENCE – JESUS' WORDS IN REAL HISTORY!
Many skeptics question whether Jesus' words were truly spoken or simply added later. However, both historical records and biblical archaeology confirm them.

📖 Luke 23:34 (KJV):
"Then said Jesus, Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do."

🔥 PROOF #1: THE EARLY CHURCH RECORDED JESUS’ PRAYER!
❓ READER QUESTION:
"Brother John, how do we know for sure that Jesus actually spoke these words?"

📌 The Gospel of Luke, which records these words, was written by Luke—a doctor and historian. Early Christian writings from church fathers such as Irenaeus (130-202 AD) and Justin Martyr (100-165 AD) also referenced this event, confirming that Jesus' prayer of forgiveness was widely known among early believers.

🔗 Proof from Early Church Fathers – Irenaeus & Justin Martyr
👉 https://www.newadvent.org/fathers/
🚨 THE WARNING: If the early church confirmed it, why do modern skeptics doubt it?

🔥 PROOF #2: ROMAN RECORDS CONFIRM JESUS’ CRUCIFIXION!
❓ READER QUESTION:
"Brother John, do non-Christian historical sources confirm Jesus’ crucifixion?"

📖 Tacitus, a Roman historian (AD 56-120), wrote:
"Christus, from whom the name [Christian] had its origin, suffered the extreme penalty during the reign of Tiberius, at the hands of one of our procurators, Pontius Pilatus."
📌 This confirms that Jesus’ crucifixion was a real historical event—and His words of forgiveness were spoken in a documented moment of history.

🔗 Tacitus’ Writings on Jesus – Roman Historical Records
👉 https://www.worldhistory.org/Tacitus/
🚨 THE WARNING: Even the enemies of Christianity confirmed Jesus’ death—so why do people still deny it today?

POWERFUL PRAYER FOR A HEART OF FORGIVENESS!
This prayer is for those who struggle with forgiveness and want to have a heart like Jesus.
🙏 🔥 PRAY THIS OUT LOUD:

"Father, I thank You for the incredible forgiveness You showed on the cross. Help me to forgive as You have forgiven me. When others hurt me, let me respond with mercy instead of anger. Remove any bitterness from my heart and fill me with the love of Christ. Give me the strength to pray for my enemies and to walk in true grace. I surrender my heart to You and ask for Your Spirit to work in me. In Jesus’ name, AMEN!"
